patches.summary: Retry loop honours Retry-After on 429/503 (cap 30 s, up to 50% jitter), replays only GET/HEAD or CLI-keyed allowlisted mutations, bounds every call with a 120 s budget, and prints one gate_busy line.
patches.reason: The generated loop retried every method on 5xx and network errors after a fixed 1/2/4 s and ignored Retry-After, which replays mutations and amplifies the API's gate_busy queue (Codex found it 2026-10-14).
patches.validated_outcome: Unkeyed POST gets exactly one request on 429, 5xx, a dropped connection, a body reset and a 307; a warm-connection POST with a user Idempotency-Key header is still sent once with the header stripped.
patches.upstream_issue: To file against mvanhorn/cli-printing-press: never retry non-idempotent verbs on 429/5xx/network errors, honour Retry-After on 5xx, offer a per-call budget.

patches.summary: Redirect rules (a mutation is never sent to another origin; cross-origin GET/HEAD forwards only an allowlist of headers) and request-aware credential redaction (headers, cookies, query, fragment, secret path codes, JSON/multipart bodies, redirect targets, Referer/Link) with a lazy, budgeted mask set that withholds output when it overflows. Redaction keeps the original error class (errors.Is/As to url.Error, net.OpError, DNSError with masked text) so the local-data fallback still works; MCP path parameters are PathEscape-d; doctor, dry-run bodies and local-lookup messages are redacted. Webhook delivery and feedback endpoints are masked in errors and output (client.MaskErrorForURL / MaskURL); the cyclic-safe error identity walk is budgeted. Reprint 637: the two new public paths with a secret path code (/public/screen-share/{code}/state, /webhooks/inbound/forms/{token}) are in sensitivePathParams and their envelopes mask the path.
patches.reason: Error bodies, error text, URLs and envelopes echo what the server or the redirect chain returns, so credentials sent in headers, bodies, query strings or path codes could reach the terminal, logs or an external redirect target.
patches.validated_outcome: A 308 to another origin for a keyed POST sends nothing; an echoed Authorization, X-API-Key, cookie, password, token array, Location/Referer token or screen-share code never appears in APIError, err.Error(), stderr, dry-run or the JSON envelopes; with more than 256 secrets the output is withheld.
patches.upstream_issue: To file against mvanhorn/cli-printing-press: client-level redirect policy and secret redaction as generator features; path-parameter secrecy as spec metadata (x-secret) so generated envelopes mask it.

patches.summary: integrations post-slack-settings takes typed --channel and --notify-events flags (board #578; app route changed under small563). A flag that was not passed is not sent (keep); an explicit empty value (--notify-events "" or =, --channel "") is sent as [] / "" via Changed() (clear); Long states keep / clear / 400; --stdin passes the body through untouched and reads cmd.InOrStdin(). spec.yaml and upstream/openapi.yaml carry the live typed requestBody. Prose note: .printing-press-patches/slack-settings-typed-body-578.md. Since reprint 637 both files are the whole live document.
patches.reason: The generated command was printed from the untyped body, so it offered only --stdin; a reprint from the untyped spec, or a hand edit that drops Changed(), would silently send nothing or drop the explicit empty list, which the API reads as clear-every-event.
patches.validated_outcome: Wire body is exactly the flags passed ({}, {channel}, {notifyEvents:[]} for an explicit empty value, both); --stdin bodies (including a non-array notifyEvents) reach the API unchanged for its 400; spec.yaml and upstream/openapi.yaml requestBody are deep-equal and typed; TestSpecMatchesUpstreamPublicAPI, go build, go test ./... and go vet pass.
patches.upstream_issue: None: the generator already emits typed flags from a typed body; only Long, the Changed()-gated empty-list send and InOrStdin are local.

patches.summary: conduyt-auth register takes a required --terms-accepted flag that sends termsAccepted true (board #601; POST /auth/register requires it since #575). The command takes no positional arguments (pflag reads `--terms-accepted false` as the bare flag plus a stray "false"; that spelling is refused locally, nothing sent). Without the flag (or with --terms-accepted=false) the command refuses locally, naming the Terms and Privacy Policy, and sends nothing; --stdin passes the body through untouched (reads cmd.InOrStdin()). spec.yaml and upstream/openapi.yaml carry the live requestBody. Prose note: .printing-press-patches/register-terms-accepted-601.md. Since reprint 637 both files are the whole live document.
patches.reason: A reprint from the old spec would drop the flag and every CLI registration would answer 400.
patches.validated_outcome: With --terms-accepted the wire body carries termsAccepted true; without it (or =false) no request is sent and the error names the terms; spec.yaml and upstream/openapi.yaml requestBody are deep-equal and require termsAccepted; TestSpecMatchesUpstreamPublicAPI, go build and go test ./... pass.
patches.upstream_issue: None: the generator emits a bool flag from the const-true property; only the required-true local refusal, Long and InOrStdin are local.

patches.summary: A property required INSIDE an optional nested body object is checked only when a flag of that object group was passed (nestedFlagGroupChanged), so bare `settings update` flags, `conduyt-auth logout`, `screen-share delete-session-code <code>` and the other generated commands with optional nested objects are not refused locally; `conduyt-auth logout` keeps running bare (no help guard) and `--marks-drew 0` / `--screen-share-marks-drew 0` are sent.
patches.reason: Printing Press 4.28.0 turns every nested `required` into an always-required flag. On the full public document that made `conduyt-auth logout` and `screen-share delete-session-code` unusable without screen-share flags the API does not require, and `settings update` required 19 nested flags.
patches.validated_outcome: Bare delete-session-code and logout send no nested object; one flag of a group without its required sibling is refused before any request; a full group sends drew 0. TestNestedRequiredFlagsOnlyWhenTheObjectIsSent.
patches.upstream_issue: To file against mvanhorn/cli-printing-press: a nested required list applies only when its parent object is present; int fields of a nested object are sent when Changed, not when non-zero.

patches.summary: Full reprint on the live public document (948 operations) by a 3-way merge of the 4.28.0 print onto this tree; deals list keeps its curated status/sort/order enums and defaults and refuses every non-forwarded flag in board-snapshot mode; contacts list pages on per_page and sends the limit alias only when --limit is passed (the print paged on limit=50 next to --per-page, a 400 when they differ); email send-bulk checks the newly declared replyTo/sendDomainId patterns. Prose note: .printing-press-patches/reprint-637-full-public-api.md (method, carried curation, the full dropped-content list).
patches.reason: The print had fallen 114 operations behind the public document, and the September reprint left its new top-level groups unregistered in root.go and absent from code_orch.go.
patches.validated_outcome: TestSpecMatchesUpstreamPublicAPI green on 948 operations; go build, go vet and go test ./... pass; every earlier patch test passes.
patches.upstream_issue: None for the merge itself; see nested-required-flags-637.

patches.summary: Restores the free-form JSON body flags the full reprint dropped as a generator artefact (activities create-activity --metadata, automations update --trigger-conditions, bulk edit-contacts/edit-deals --updates, contacts create --custom-fields, forms create --settings, integrations connect --config/--credentials, scoring-rules create --condition) and the seven typed flags of emails create-template beside --body-json; each sends the parsed JSON under its body key as before and refuses to mix with the generated sub-flags. Prose note: .printing-press-patches/reprint-637-freeform-json-flags.md.
patches.reason: 4.28.0 prints an object with declared sub-properties as sub-flags only and a oneOf body as --body-json only, so a reprint on the full public document removed flags existing users had while the API still reads the same keys.
patches.validated_outcome: Every restored flag is registered and its JSON lands deep-equal under its body key; malformed JSON names the flag; mixing with a sub-flag sends nothing; create-template typed flags send the pre-reprint body. TestFreeformJSONFlagsLandInTheBodyAsBefore, TestEmailsCreateTemplateTypedFlagsAsBefore.
patches.upstream_issue: For the press board (not filed): keep a whole-object JSON flag next to sub-property flags.

patches.summary: Every public array query parameter (9 on spec.yaml at reprint 637: email, tag, tagId on contacts list, contacts get-count, contacts export) is a repeatable StringArrayVar flag sent as one key per value via appendRepeatableArrayQueryParam; the literal --cf-key flag (cf[<key>]) is not registered and its MCP bindings are removed; --cf stays the documented custom-field filter. Prose note: .printing-press-patches/reprint-637-repeatable-array-query-params.md.
patches.reason: 4.28.0 prints exploded array query params as single string flags (one comma-joined value) and the deep-object cf[<key>] as a literal parameter name the API never reads.
patches.validated_outcome: For every array query param in spec.yaml the flag is a stringArray and three occurrences reach the API as repeated keys; no command registers --cf-key and the manifest has no cf[<key>]. TestEveryArrayQueryParamIsRepeatable, TestLiteralCfKeyFlagIsAbsent.
patches.upstream_issue: For the press board (not filed): emit repeatable flags for exploded array query params; skip or expand deep-object params.

patches.summary: The API dry_run query parameter is the local flag --server-dry-run on all 161 commands that have it (plus calls link call-to-contact and imports repair post-imports-id for their body dry-run); no command registers a local --dry-run (import <resource> uses the global one), so the global --dry-run always prints and sends nothing. email send/send-bulk unchanged (exempt). Prose note: .printing-press-patches/reprint-637-server-dry-run.md.
patches.reason: 4.28.0 prints dry_run as a local --dry-run that shadows the global preview, so a requested local preview sent a real request on 153 pre-existing commands after the full reprint.
patches.validated_outcome: No local --dry-run anywhere in the tree; --server-dry-run bound on every dry_run operation but the two email ones; the global --dry-run on each of them sends zero requests. TestNoLocalDryRunAndServerDryRunIsBound.
patches.upstream_issue: For the press board (not filed): never emit a local flag that shadows a persistent root flag.
